segments.title: FREMM modularity and Constellation's system changes
segments.body: FREMM accommodates different configurations through a modular design. Most users have been willing to work within its intended arrangements. The criticism of Constellation is that it selected this adaptable design, then sought its own systems and reconfigured the ship around them. That approach creates further design work by departing from the modules and compatible systems intended to support adaptation.

evidence.note: FREMM's adaptable modular design supports different configurations, and most users have been willing to work within its intended arrangements.
The criticism of Constellation centres on choosing new systems and reconfiguring the ship around them after selecting an adaptable modular design.

segments.summary: FREMM's modularity frames a criticism of Constellation: replacing the intended systems can require extensive changes to the design chosen for its adaptability.

segments.title: Why air-conditioning connections can force wider ship changes
segments.body: Air-conditioning units can be roughly the same size while placing their intake and power connections in different positions. Those differences require the surrounding connections to be rerouted. Repeating such substitutions across the ship adds further changes to its systems. Small alterations can consequently accumulate into extensive reconfiguration of the ship's hull.

evidence.note: Air-conditioning units of roughly similar size can have intakes and power supplies in different positions, requiring rerouting. Repeated substitutions illustrate how small system changes accumulate into extensive hull reconfiguration.

segments.summary: Roughly similar-sized air-conditioning units can place intake and power connections differently, forcing rerouting that accumulates into wider changes to the ship.
